comparison.text: In the US, today's air would be officially rated 'Moderate'. Here it is called Tuesday.
comparison.source_name: US EPA, Technical Assistance Document for the Reporting of Daily Air Quality (AirNow, 2024 breakpoints)
comparison.caveat: US categories use the same pollutant with stricter cut points than India's AQI, which is why the same air sounds scarier in American.

comparison.text: A NIOSH N95 removes at least 95 percent of airborne particles when it seals to your face. On days like this, it is not paranoia, it is arithmetic.
comparison.source_name: CDC NIOSH, Proper N95 Respirator Use (Science Bulletin)
comparison.caveat: The 95 percent is the certified filter performance with a proper seal. Beards, gaps and surgical masks do not deliver it.

comparison.text: Kids breathe faster than adults, so they absorb more of this per kilo. They also live closer to the ground, where some pollutants peak. WHO's words, not ours.
comparison.source_name: WHO, More than 90% of the world's children breathe toxic air every day (2018)
comparison.caveat: Direct WHO statements: children 'breathe more rapidly than adults and so absorb more pollutants' and 'live closer to the ground, where some pollutants reach peak concentrations'.

comparison.text: The most polluted city on Earth in the 2025 IQAir report is Loni, in Delhi NCR: 112.5 ug/m3 average, 22x the WHO limit. All 25 worst cities were in India, Pakistan and China.
comparison.source_name: IQAir, 2025 World Air Quality Report press release
comparison.caveat: IQAir rankings blend government and low-cost sensor data and only cover cities that measure at all. Plenty of unmonitored places never make the list.

comparison.text: Breathing Nashik air today = smoking 0.5 cigarettes. No lighter needed.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence (Richard A. Muller and Elizabeth A. Muller)
comparison.caveat: A rule of thumb comparing health effects, not identical smoke. The authors call it a rough estimate, and unlike smoking, polluted air is breathed by everyone including kids.
